missionPremise: The dispatch's own framing: this is the second time in one day the pin-vs-bake-reach seam has held up the same counties (CTX-SITUS-SKIP merged, the pin stayed put, and Caldwell/McLennan failed on a fix that was merged and unreachable). Item 1 bumps the pin to LDT main and PROVES the change reaches /app/bakes rather than assuming it (Dockerfile.publish copies only /ldt/node_modules and /app/bakes, an esbuild bundle over a ~26-module graph). Item 2 replaces the person-noticing mechanism with a mechanical check, explicitly barred from being 'pin differs from LDT main' (named worse than nothing -- the pin is supposed to lag) and required instead to fire only when a commit in the gap touches a file inside the bake's own module graph.
completionPredicate: Pin bumped to LDT main with a provenance comment matching the file's established style; the bump's bake-reach traced and reported (including what is NOT picked up, not just what is); a committed, reusable module-graph tracer; a committed _LDT_SHA shape guard; a committed staleness check implementing the meaning-shaped rule; all three violation cases (fail at old pin, pass at new pin, pass on a real non-bake-graph divergence) and the two shape-guard cases demonstrated with literal output and process exit codes, plus permanent node:test regressions so the demonstration can't silently rot; a deliberate, justified CI-vs-script placement decision with reachability established by a real run, not analogy alone; all of it merged to main with CI conclusion string 'success'.
scopeBasis: Two files only in cloudbuild.publish.yaml's blast radius: the _LDT_SHA line + its comment. cloudbuild.parcel-r5-zoning.yaml's pin explicitly excluded per dispatch (false provenance label, not a stale dependency, gates four counties -- left as a leave_behind, not touched). ci.yml explicitly NOT touched for the new check (see checkDesign below) -- the check lives in its own workflow file instead, a boundary I drew myself and am reporting for review, not one the dispatch stated. No deploys, Cloud Build submissions, or Cloud Run job executions performed, per dispatch's explicit prohibition; the integration seat rebuilds from merged main and runs the counties.

item2_stalenessCheckDesign.rejectedDesign: _LDT_SHA !== LDT main -> fail. Explicitly named worse than nothing: fires on nearly every check since the pin is supposed to lag and most LDT commits never touch the bake; trains the fleet to bypass the control.
item2_stalenessCheckDesign.adoptedDesign: fail only when the net tree diff between the pinned SHA and the target (LDT main by default) contains a path that is a member of the bake module graph computed at the target commit. Net diff (git diff --name-only, not a per-commit union) so a change reverted within the range does not falsely fire.

ciPlacementDecision.decision: Both a standalone script AND an automated CI workflow -- but a dedicated workflow (.github/workflows/ldt-pin-staleness.yml), not a job inside ci.yml.
ciPlacementDecision.whyNotCiYml: ci.yml triggers on every branch push and every PR fleet-wide (`on: push: branches: ['**']` / `pull_request`). This check's subject is LDT's own commit history, entirely independent of what any given hauska-factory PR changes. Wiring it into the everything-gate would let LDT drifting on its own silently block unrelated lane merges -- the same over-broad-control failure the dispatch names for the check's LOGIC, just moved to the check's BLAST RADIUS. I drew this scope boundary myself; it is not stated in the dispatch, and I'm flagging it explicitly per DEV_PROCESS 5.4 (structural/policy calls are for the operator to confirm or override, not for a lane to decide silently) in case the integration seat wants it wired in as a hard merge gate instead.
ciPlacementDecision.chosenTriggers: push to main (post-merge monitoring), a 6-hour cron schedule (catches drift purely from LDT's own movement with zero hauska-factory activity -- the exact CTX-SITUS-SKIP shape), and workflow_dispatch (on demand before dispatching a publish build)
